system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal and privileged. Buyer-side analysis only.

## 1. Headline assessment

The Seller describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. **Nearly every key position sits at or beyond our fallback, and several go well past it.** Three structural features would strip value from the warranty package even before the headline numbers are considered:

1. Clause 12.3 extends the limitations "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise", and clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 do the same for limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is the hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits.
2. General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2) is combined with a blanket buyer-knowledge bar extending to anything "discoverable" (cl 8.3).
3. Title and capacity would sit inside the general cap and the 18-month limit.

Together these would largely neutralise the warranties on exactly the issues the Disclosure Letter itself flags: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses and the DD-006 incident.

There is also a factual inconsistency we should use. The Seller Update says Bluefen is "addressed", Riverlark will be dealt with by release, and the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics". The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (DL 2, 3 and 5) confirms that:
- no Bluefen consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists;
- Riverlark has not been repaid or discharged; and
- the AUD 420,000 bonuses are absent from the funds flow.

**Authority point:** No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for any fallback, including the 20% cap, the 18-month period and a post-Completion Riverlark release. Our mark-up must go back at our starting positions. Nothing in this memo should be read as authorising a concession.

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability regime

| # | Seller position | Playbook | Gap | Push-back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cap (12.1):** 20%, AUD 4.8m | 25%, AUD 6.0m. 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft | The Seller has opened at our authority-gated fallback | Reinstate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is available. Escalate to Amelia only if the team later wants authority. |
| 2 | **De minimis (12.2):** AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x | Reinstate AUD 5,000. Related or recurring claims should aggregate so they count towards the de minimis. |
| 3 | **Basket (12.2):** AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar (tipping) | 5x, and it is a deductible rather than a tipping basket | Reinstate AUD 50,000 tipping basket. A deductible on a AUD 250,000 basket is about 1% of price permanently uncovered. |
| 4 | **General claims period (12.3):** 18 months | 24 months. 18 months is an authority-gated fallback (none given) | At fallback without authority | Reinstate 24 months. |
| 5 | **Universal limitation (12.3):** "any limitation…applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep categories separate. No hidden override | This would sweep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants, payment obligations and fraud into the general regime by default | Delete. Reverse the default so that general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims. Each other category gets its own expressly stated regime. |
| 6 | **Fundamental/Title:** same caps and limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Fundamental departure | Reject outright. Title and capacity go to the heart of the deal. A AUD 4.8m cap on a AUD 24m share title claim leaves us exposed for 80% of the price. "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. |
| 7 | **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5):** apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable | No fraud carve-out at all | Insert an express carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable and not waivable by anyone on the team. Also confirm that non-reliance does not exclude reliance on the express warranties and Disclosure Letter. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**8. General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2).**
- The letter purports to disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- The playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure.
- The words "or referred to" are especially broad. They would disclose matters only cross-referenced in a document.

*Push-back:* Delete 1.1 and 1.2 entirely. Disclosure should be against specific warranties only, and fairly disclosed with enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact. The data room can be referenced only where a specific disclosure expressly incorporates a named document.

**9. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** This is a blanket bar covering anything known to the Buyer "or its advisers", including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- It combines a knowledge bar with constructive knowledge.
- Taken with item 8, it would bar claims on almost every DD-flagged issue.
- It also captures adviser knowledge, which we cannot practically police.

*Push-back:* Delete 8.3. If any qualifier survives, it should work the other way: Seller awareness qualifiers limited to named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. We should also consider an express statement that Buyer knowledge or investigation does not limit claims (pro-sandbagging).

**10. Non-admission (DL 1.4).** A standard non-admission is tolerable. We must make sure it cannot be read to dilute the factual disclosures in DL 2–10. Those are useful to us because they confirm the gaps.

**11. Staleness.** The letter speaks "as at 22 September 2026". Today is 6 November 2026. We need:
- a refreshed letter;
- warranties repeated at Completion, with any update disclosure for the period between signing and Completion not curing breaches, or at least giving us termination or claim rights; and
- confirmation of whether the data-room cut-off has moved.

### C. Conditions and Completion mechanics

**12. Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3, DL 2).**
- This is our most material customer: about AUD 3.6m in FY26 revenue, roughly 30%.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied merely on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- DL 2 confirms that no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions under clause 11.3 exists.
- Satisfaction on delivery could leave us with a "consent" that is subject to unmet conditions and therefore not yet effective. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient under the playbook.

*Push-back:* The Completion condition should be an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2. It should come with documentary evidence that each clause 11.3 condition has been satisfied, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably, and be delivered before Completion. We should also seek:
- a stronger efforts standard, such as best or all reasonable endeavours with defined steps;
- Buyer review of, and consultation on, any Seller communications with Bluefen; and
- a Buyer walk right if the condition is not met by the sunset date.

**13. Riverlark (cl 2 / 7, DL 3).**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.
- The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is in hand.
- A change of control would likely trigger clause 8.1, so leaving this unresolved at Completion is a real risk.

*Push-back:* Require:
- a current payout letter from Riverlark;
- direct repayment out of Completion funds, deducted from the price as Debt; and
- executed security releases or discharges (including PPSR releases) delivered at Completion under clause 9.2.

A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither exists, so we reject that structure for now.

**14. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses (DL 5).**
- The Seller states the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" while excluding the AUD 420,000 bonuses as "a matter for the Seller".
- Unless the Seller actually pays them, the Company bears them after Completion. That cost lands on us.
- DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- The playbook prohibits a funds flow that silently excludes these items.

*Push-back:* Either:
- (a) itemise the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation if applicable, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation and similar) as a specific funds-flow line item and treat them as Debt or a Transaction Expense deducted from price; or
- (b) have them Seller-funded, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general limitations.

We also need the bonus terms, a confirmed recipient list and the payroll mechanics, including whether any amounts survive if a condition fails.

### D. Specific risk areas

**15. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1, DL 4).**
- The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment.
- DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but there is no independent bank verification either way, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- The real risk is not just the payment. It is that the Company does not own IP it may be relying on.

*Push-back:* Keep the SOW3 cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable. Broaden the indemnity to cover:
- any loss from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 Project Materials;
- Ironquay claims; and
- remediation or replacement costs.

The indemnity should sit outside the general cap, basket and time limit. We should not assume the AUD 180,000 figure is either correct or wrong. Ask for bank statements and Ironquay's statement of account to verify the amount.

**16. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6, DL 6).**
- The Seller calls this "preliminary operational… not expected to be material".
- DL 6 says the scope, any access by unauthorised persons and any notification obligation are all unestablished.
- The approach is to assume neither a confirmed breach nor that there is nothing to worry about.

*Push-back:* Do not accept the materiality characterisation into the operative SPA. Require:
- preservation of all logs and evidence, including link access logs and email delivery records;
- the investigation to continue diligently, with regular written updates to the Buyer before Completion and access to the investigator;
- Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual notification decision, or any public statement;
- a privacy and data warranty that is not diluted by the general disclosure; and
- consideration of a specific indemnity or conditional protection if the investigation later establishes an eligible data breach. This should be framed contingently, with no assumed quantum.

We should make no numeric demand on this issue at this stage.

**17. Sandbar supplier renewals (DL 8; DD-008 / DD-011).**
- There are three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 in total.
- The Seller asserts they are ordinary course. DL 8 itself says it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that the documents should be read together for timing and scope.

*Push-back:* Neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor assume Debt treatment. Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights and accrual treatment. Assess whether any portion relates to a pre-Completion period, or was entered or renewed outside the ordinary course, for example linked to the sale. Reserve the position on working capital or Debt treatment pending that analysis. No automatic price deduction.

**18. Tax and IP warranties.** The Seller claims these are "settled under the general regime". They are not. Both remain **open** under our playbook. Respond that the Tax and IP regimes are under negotiation and are not agreed under the general cap or time limits. Make no assumption of unlimited liability, and no resolution in either direction. This also ties back to item 5: the universal-limitation drafting must not settle these by default.

**19. Title (DL 10, DD-012).** The Seller relies on the Company's own share register. DL 10 candidly concedes that this is the source relied on, not Buyer verification. Under the playbook, the internal register is not independent proof. *Require:*
- ASIC company extract and historical searches reconciled to the register;
- the share issue and transfer history, with board minutes and stamp duty where relevant;
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
- constitution and shareholder agreement pre-emption waivers;
- Seller authority evidence (board resolution and capacity); and
- title and capacity warranties within the separate Fundamental regime (item 6).

**20. Lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9).** The Seller states that the lease involves only a notification obligation and that the Mossvale restriction is triggered by assignment, not a share sale. These are not playbook items, but they are factual characterisations that we should **verify independently**. Check DD-007 and DD-009 for change-of-control, "deemed assignment" or similar clauses. Diarise the lease notification as a Completion or post-Completion action.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Reject and return to starting position. No fallback authority exists.**
1. Cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Reject 20%.
2. De minimis: AUD 5,000. Basket: AUD 50,000, tipping and first-dollar.
3. General claims period: 24 months. Reject 18 months.
4. Fundamental/Title: separate regime with a 100% cap, at least 6 years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
6. Delete the universal-limitation language in 12.3 and the "all Claims of any nature" language in 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5. Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant categories separate.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
7. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Specific fair disclosure only.
8. Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar. Any qualifier should be named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, with carve-outs for title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.
9. Require a refreshed Disclosure Letter and a bring-down at Completion.

**Completion deliverables**
10. Bluefen: an effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone.
11. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and executed security releases at Completion. Reject post-Completion release.
12. Bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs as an express funds-flow line item or Debt deduction, or Seller-funded with a specific indemnity.

**Specific protections**
13. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment while preserving the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment). Verify the AUD 180,000 rather than assume it.
14. DD-006: preservation, continuing investigation, updates, Buyer consultation and an undiluted privacy warranty. Assume no breach, harm, notification duty or quantum.
15. Sandbar: request documents and assess. No automatic Debt or price deduction.
16. Tax and IP: respond that these remain open and are not settled under the general regime.
17. Title: independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, transfer history, authority). DD-012 alone is insufficient.
18. Lease and Mossvale: verify the Seller's characterisations against the underlying documents.

**Tactical note:** In the covering response, highlight the gap between the Seller Update and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter on Bluefen, Riverlark and the funds flow. This lets us press for Completion deliverables without arguing the facts. We should also avoid signalling where our fallbacks sit. Any move towards a 20% cap, an 18-month period or a deferred Riverlark release needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies the specific draft.
=== END ADVICE ===
